rv.q: Achieving that in this kind of play, though, requires more of a surrogate parental relationship between these two characters and that needs two actors who more clearly occupy the same world and find a mutual way to drive on through its thickets.
Six Men Dressed Like Joseph Stalin is funny, tragic, and a love letter to theater, as well as a political history lesson.
Six Men Dressed Like Joseph Stalin is a show ripe with ideas to contemplate, and it's wonderful if only to watch these two men world build for us in a deep way.
Cruz and Judd bring endearing and touching chemistry to Nora's characters, even when the script feels like it's veering into clever-for-its-own-sake territory.
"Six Men Dressed Like Joseph Stalin" is a play well worth seeing—if not for its acting then its writing, intriguing set design, and creative direction...
But for me, there is not much in the emotional engagement that might be expected.
